system_overview: This specification models the Disk Synod (Disk Paxos) algorithm by Gafni and Lamport (2003), which implements distributed consensus using shared disks instead of separate acceptor processes. Processes communicate by reading and writing blocks on a set of shared disks. The algorithm operates in phases: a recovery phase (phase 0), a preparation phase (phase 1, analogous to Paxos phase 1), and an acceptance phase (phase 2, analogous to Paxos phase 2). Progress requires a majority of disks to be accessible, and the algorithm tolerates arbitrary process crashes.
actors_and_components: The system consists of: (1) A set of N processes, each identified by a number, that propose values and attempt to reach consensus. Each process owns a unique set of ballot numbers. (2) A set of shared disks, where each disk stores a block for each process. Blocks contain a master ballot number, a ballot number, and an input value. (3) A majority quorum requirement on the disk set: any two sets of disks that each constitute a majority must overlap.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) Input mapping: each process's current proposed input value. (2) Output mapping: each process's output (either a chosen value or a no-output indicator). (3) Disk state: for each disk and each process, a block containing a master ballot number, a ballot number, and an input value (or a no-input indicator). (4) Phase: each process is in phase 0 (recovery), 1 (preparation), 2 (acceptance), or 3 (output produced). (5) A local disk block for each process, containing the same three fields as a disk block. (6) A set of disks written: which disks each process has written to in the current phase. (7) Blocks read: for each process and each disk, the set of blocks read from other processes on that disk.
initial_state: Each process starts with a nondeterministically chosen input value. All outputs are set to the no-output indicator. All disk blocks are initialized with zero ballot numbers and the no-input indicator. All processes start in phase 0. Each process's local disk block is initialized to zeroes and no-input. No disks have been written to. No blocks have been read.
actions: The protocol actions are: (1) Start ballot: A process in phase 1 or 2 begins a new ballot by selecting a ballot number higher than its current master ballot, resetting to phase 1, and clearing its written/read tracking. (2) Phase 1 or 2 write: A process writes its local disk block to a disk, recording the disk as written. (3) Phase 1 or 2 read: A process reads another process's block from a disk it has already written to. If the read block has a master ballot at least as high as the process's own, the process must start a new ballot. Otherwise, the block is recorded. (4) End phase 1: When a process has written to and read from a majority of disks, it sets its ballot equal to its master ballot and selects an input value -- either its own input (if no block with a non-initial input was read) or the input from the block with the highest ballot among those read. Then it advances to phase 2. (5) End phase 2: When the same majority condition is met, the process outputs its input value and advances to phase 3. (6) Fail: A process crashes, resets to phase 0 with a fresh input, clears its local block to the initial state, clears its output, and resets tracking state. Its data on the disks persists. (7) Phase 0 read: A recovering process reads its own block from a disk. (8) End phase 0: When the process has read its own block from a majority of disks, it selects a new ballot number higher than any master ballot it saw, restores the block with the highest ballot, sets the master ballot to the new one, and enters phase 1.
safety_properties: Consensus: The specification implements the abstract Synod specification, guaranteeing that at most one value is chosen, and all processes that output must output the same value. Any chosen value was originally proposed by some process.
model_bounds: N processes, a finite set of valid inputs, a finite set of disks, and a majority predicate must be supplied as constants. Ballot numbers for each process must be disjoint positive natural numbers.
additional_assumptions: Each process has a unique set of ballot numbers, and these sets are pairwise disjoint. The majority quorum property is assumed: the full disk set is a majority, and any two majority subsets intersect. The specification extends the abstract Synod module and is proven to implement the Synod specification (DiskSynodSpec implies SynodSpec).
